description: W2V-focused physical-dynamics shortcut slice with overlapping object sets so process words are cued by local evidence rather than object identity.
notes: Generate 200 documents: 25 each for fall, rise, sink, float, speed_up, slow_down, roll, and slide.
Each concept has seven scenario frames. Object sets intentionally recur across different concepts with different mechanisms.
This is a diagnostic Word2Vec slice: short active sentences, target term plus evidence cue in the same sentence, and minimal object-only shortcuts.

physical_dynamics_profile.definition: Can a model connect evidence about directional physical change, motion, and state/process change over time to the right event/process concept?
physical_dynamics_profile.centrality_rule: The target process and its local evidence cue must be close together; overlapping object sets should make the mechanism and evidence, not object identity, carry the meaning.
generation_guidance: Write short active observations, not definitions or benchmark-style examples.
Put the lexical target and its evidence cue in the same sentence whenever possible.
Keep opposite-polarity evidence out of the document.
Use the object as the grammatical subject of the target process.
Do not imply that one object always has one outcome; use the cause and evidence fields to disambiguate.

path_shape_policy.guidance: Use path_shape as a compact cue only when natural.

document_types.description: A short active observation with target and evidence in one sentence.
A compact play-by-play description of a visible physical change.

families.label: W2V object-agnostic lexical shortcuts
families.schema: Short active examples pair each process term with a nearby evidence cue while reusing object sets across different process outcomes.

discourse_styles.description: A short plain sentence where the object does the target process and the evidence appears nearby.
guidance: Write one or two short active sentences.
Use the object as the subject of the target process.
Put the lexical target and the shortcut evidence in the same sentence.
Let the cause or mechanism distinguish this object from other possible outcomes.
Avoid definition chains and avoid the word means.

discourse_styles.description: A compact watching-it-happen description of a visible physical change.
guidance: Write like someone is watching the motion happen.
Use simple active wording with now, as, or while only when natural.
Keep the target process and visual evidence close together.
Let the local evidence, not object identity, explain the process.
Avoid formal explanation and avoid contrast language.
